cards.explanation: The answer is the priests and the prophets. The men from Bethel ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Hosts, and the prophets too (Zechariah 7:3). They sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, so this wasn't a casual question over the fence, friends. Their question was about weeping and fasting in the fifth month.

The answer is True. The LORD tells Zechariah to ask all the people of the land and the priests (Zechariah 7:5). Notice that it's not only the priests, friends. The question is for everybody, and nobody gets to sit this one out.

The answer is whether it was really for Him. God asks, "…was it really for Me that you fasted?" (Zechariah 7:5). Seventy years of fasting and mourning, and He puts one question on the table. It's not about the calendar, friends. It's about who the fasting was for.

The answer is the prophets. God says these are the words He proclaimed through the earlier prophets (Zechariah 7:7). Zechariah isn't bringing some brand new idea, friends. The message was already out there, and God is pointing back to it.

The answer is False. The verse says Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were populous and prosperous (Zechariah 7:7). The Negev and the foothills were inhabited too. So the places were busy, not empty, friends. It's a lot like a bakery on cookie day, with every counter taken.
The answer is True. The LORD of Hosts says, "Administer true justice." (Zechariah 7:9). It's the first thing on the list, friends. Straight, plain and no loopholes.

The answer is oppress. God says, "Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor." (Zechariah 7:10). He names four groups, and nobody is left guessing who He means. To oppress means to press down on someone, and He says don't.

The answer is False. The text says they "…refused to pay attention and turned a stubborn shoulder; they stopped up their ears from hearing." (Zechariah 7:11). That's three ways of saying no in one verse, friends. These were not people leaning in to listen.

The answer is that their hearts were hard and unbending. The text says "They made their hearts like flint and would not listen…" (Zechariah 7:12). Flint is a hard stone, and you can't bend it. It's a picture of hearts that wouldn't give an inch, friends. I've met dough like that on a cold morning, but this is much more serious.

The answer is that He would not listen, and it's a heavy verse. The LORD says, "And just as I had called and they would not listen, so when they called I would not listen…" (Zechariah 7:13). The way they treated His call came back around. I think this is one of the hard parts to read, so take a breath with me, friends.

The answer is among nations they had not known. The LORD says He scattered them "…with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known…" (Zechariah 7:14). I think that's a hard way to be scattered, friends.

The answer is desolate. The verse says "…the land was left desolate behind them so that no one could come or go." (Zechariah 7:14). Desolate means empty and deserted. It's a sad picture of a land that used to be full, friends.
